# Scientific Calculator

> A free scientific calculator that works offline: fractions, trigonometry, logarithms, 102 formulas and 59 constants, a unit converter, a graph, a solver, finance, statistics, matrices and complex numbers, and a history of past calculations, exported as text or CSV. Nothing leaves your browser.

A static web app (no account, no server, no tracking): everything is calculated in the browser. Installable as an app on iOS, Android and desktop. Also available as a Chrome extension.

## Links
- [Calculator](https://raad.dev/calculator/): the app, with options and a guide to every function
- [For schools and organizations](https://raad.dev/calculator/admin): turning features of the Chrome extension off for students, from the Google Admin Console
- [Source code and documentation](https://github.com/raad-altaie/scientific-calculator): README, tests, AGPL-3.0 license

## Facts
- Precision: about 15 significant digits (IEEE 754 doubles), shown to 13.
- Angle units: degrees, radians, gradians. Fraction mode. Fix, Sci and Eng formats.
- Panels: formulas and constants; unit converter (28 kinds, with force, torque, density, frequency, flow rate, momentum, radioactivity, magnetic field and electrical units: current, voltage, charge, resistance, capacitance, inductance), with days between dates, dates moved on, Unix timestamps and time zones; graph (functions, sliders, roots and crossings, areas, derivatives, equations and inequalities of x and y, polar and parametric curves, recursive and explicit sequences, slope fields with their solutions, best fits); solver (roots of equations in exact form as well, inequalities, turning points, polynomials, linear systems, two curves, integrals, sums to infinity, limits, Taylor series, areas between curves, arc lengths, differential equations, time value of money (N, I/Y, PV, PMT, FV), NPV, IRR and payback, loan payment schedules, savings growth, APR and APY, bond price and yield, depreciation, break-even, inflation, percentage change and markup, normal, t, chi-squared, F, binomial, Poisson, geometric, hypergeometric, exponential and uniform distributions, confidence intervals; geometry: triangle solver, shapes, solids, points and lines, circle through three points, polygon area); each card of the solver, numbers, chemistry, physics, statistics tests and dates with an Example, and a graph first in its results where one fits; statistics (mean, median, quartiles, standard deviation, variance, mode, histogram and box plot; pairs with linear, quadratic, cubic, exponential, power, logarithmic and logistic fits, correlation and Spearman's rho; hypothesis tests: one- and two-sample t, paired t, z, one and two proportions, chi-squared goodness of fit and independence, ANOVA, correlation); numbers (matrices up to 10 × 10 with eigenvalues, powers, row reduction, null space, LU and QR, least squares, pasted from a spreadsheet or as [1 2; 3 4], an example on each card; vectors; complex numbers in polar and exponential form, polynomials of them, AC impedance of R, L and C; bases and bits up to 128 with byte order, any base from 2 to 36, text and Unicode codes, Base32, Base58, Base64 and Base85, hashes (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512, CRC-32), UUIDs (version 4 and 7, and read), IPv4 and IPv6 subnets (CIDR), IEEE 754; prime factors, GCD and LCM, modular arithmetic, the Chinese remainder theorem, exact big numbers, primes, fractions and repeating decimals).; chemistry (the periodic table of 118 elements with the absorption and emission spectra of 98 of them, from NIST, molar mass, balancing reactions, composition, and more chemistry tools); physics (electronics: resistor colour code, series and parallel networks, Ohm's law, wire resistance, voltage dividers, LED resistors, capacitors, RC and RL circuits, parallel plates, transformers, RMS and LC resonance, electricity cost, battery life, BJT switching and bias, MOSFETs, Zener regulators, op-amps, 555 timers, E12 values; motion: SUVAT, projectiles, circular motion, pendulums and springs, rotation and moments of inertia; forces: F = ma, inclined planes, collisions, impulse, energy, work, torque and levers, gravitation, drag and terminal velocity, Coulomb's law, magnetic force, magnetic fields of wires, solenoids and loops, electromagnetic induction; waves: standing waves, lenses and mirrors, refraction, interference (double slit, diffraction grating), polarisation (Malus, Brewster), Doppler effect, photons, decibels; matter: specific and latent heat, mixing, thermal expansion, conduction, radiation, kinetic theory of gases, heat engines and Carnot efficiency, stress, strain and Young's modulus, density, pressure, buoyancy, pipe flow; modern and quantum: E = mc², nuclear binding energy, photoelectric effect, de Broglie wavelength, uncertainty principle, particle in a box, Compton scattering, quantum tunnelling, special relativity, hydrogen spectrum and Bohr model, radioactive decay; many cards drawn: graphs, rays, fringes, standing waves, energy levels).
- Author: Raad Altaie. License: AGPL-3.0.
